clue.text: It makes a man hot and sweet

definitions.text: It makes a man hot and sweet

parts.words: It makes a man hot and sweet
parts.note: a spiced biscuit dough is cut into little figures of men, flavoured with the hot spice ginger and sweetened

explanation.surface: Something that makes a man attractive and charming.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests something that makes a person sexy and kind; the 'man' is the biscuit figure, 'hot' the spice.
explanation.definitionFit: The biscuit figure baked from this ginger-spiced dough is the familiar treat shaped like a little man.

clue.text: Sign of trail-bike ruts Egyptologist's covered over

indicators.note: in a down clue over means read upwards, turning the letters back to front
the letters are covered by the words around them, sitting inside the phrase

explanation.surface: An Egyptologist has covered over the tracks of a trail bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covered' finds ERUTSEG inside 'bike ruts Egyptologist's'; 'over' turns it upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A gesture is a sign made with the hands or body.

clue.text: Conveniently taking time out for run? Not quite

indicators.note: taking one letter out and putting another in its place is a swap
out for marks the letter removed and the one that replaces it

parts.note: neatly means handily or conveniently
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Something done conveniently by skipping time for a run, not quite right.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly means almost, falling just short.

clue.text: What's represented by the fifth letter in email?

definitions.text: What's represented by the fifth letter in email?

parts.words: What's represented by the fifth letter in email?
parts.note: the fifth letter of the alphabet starts the word email, standing for the adjective describing computer-sent mail

explanation.surface: A puzzle about the letter in position five of the word email.
explanation.walkthrough: The fifth letter of 'email' is L; the fifth letter of the alphabet is E, which starts the word.
explanation.definitionFit: The E in email abbreviates the word for digital, computer-based mail.

clue.text: Dough, not doe!

definitions.meaning: a doe is a female deer, so the male one is meant

explanation.surface: A baker's pun on dough sounding like doe.
explanation.definitionFit: Buck is slang for a dollar, money, and also the male deer as opposed to the female.

clue.text: Researched old quarry used in commercial

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: the quarry is used inside the advertisement, placed within it

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
a mine is a quarry dug for minerals

explanation.surface: A historic quarry appearing in a TV advert, as researched.
explanation.definitionFit: To have examined something is to have studied or inspected it closely.

clue.text: Daughter is, y'know, showing hostility

parts.note: like is a filler word in chat, much as y'know is

explanation.surface: A daughter, sort of, showing hostility in teenage speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Dislike is a feeling of aversion or antipathy.

clue.text: Father's herbal extract?

parts.note: Pa is an informal word for father, with the possessive S
sage is a common kitchen herb, so something herbal here is sage

explanation.surface: A question about a potion or tincture made from herbs by Dad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herbal extract' reads as one phrase, but 'extract' is the definition and 'herbal' supplies the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract from a book or piece of music is a short section quoted from it, a passage.

clue.text: Pie portions mixed up, for instance

definitions.note: the word for is an instance of this part of speech

indicators.note: the letters of pie portions are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Portions of pie get mixed up, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For instance' looks like a link phrase meaning 'e.g.'; it means the word 'for' is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The word for is a typical example of a word linking a noun to the rest of a sentence.

clue.text: Model girl, one among hundreds

indicators.note: one piece sits among the others, so the girl and one go inside the hundreds

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so two hundreds give CC
lass is a word for a girl
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fashion model who is a rare beauty, one in a few hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model girl' looks like a single phrase about fashion; 'Model' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something classic is a model of its kind, an outstanding and exemplary standard.

clue.text: Brief written up after scams Edward put together

indicators.note: the reversed brief word comes after the scams

parts.note: cons are scams

indicators.note: in a down clue written up means read upwards, so back to front

parts.note: curt means brief or terse
Ted is a familiar short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A short report written up after Edward assembled scams.
explanation.definitionFit: Constructed means built or assembled from parts.

clue.text: All the same, many martyrs were asking for it

definitions.text: All the same, many martyrs were asking for it

parts.words: All the same, many martyrs were asking for it
parts.note: a state where all are the same in rights and standing is what many who died for a cause demanded

explanation.surface: A grudging remark that martyrs brought their fate on themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All the same' sounds like 'nevertheless' and 'asking for it' like blame; both are meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Equal rights for all, everyone treated the same, is the cause many campaigners suffered and died for.

clue.text: He painted it, twice going round article

indicators.note: going round means the doubled word is turned to run backwards
the word it is written twice over in a row

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An artist painted something, circling twice round an item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He painted it' reads as one statement; 'it' belongs to the wordplay, leaving 'He painted' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian Renaissance master of the 1500s was a painter, so he is one who painted.

clue.text: Expressed regret, seeing Goa spoiled when travelling

indicators.note: travelling letters move around, giving a new order of Goa and spoiled

explanation.surface: A tourist says sorry on finding Goa ruined by travellers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoiled' looks like the anagram signal; it is part of the fodder, and 'when travelling' does the mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: To apologise is to say sorry, expressing regret.

clue.text: Yankee must follow imperial order and toe the line

indicators.note: one piece follows the other, so the Yankee comes after the order

parts.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American soldier must follow orders and conform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Imperial order' looks like a command; it is the British honour, the Order of the British Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: To toe the line is to conform and do as one is told, to comply.

clue.text: Go with flattery when conversing

indicators.note: conversing means speaking, so the word for flattery is heard not read

parts.note: a compliment is a piece of flattering praise

explanation.surface: Advice to use flattering talk in conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: To complement something is to go well with it, completing or suiting it.

clue.text: Case of rogue compiler — passes on solutions

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: the compiler refers to the setter, me
dies means passes on, as in death

explanation.surface: A wicked crossword setter passes on answers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compiler' as ME is a crossword convention for the setter speaking of themself.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedies are cures, solutions to problems.

clue.text: Absurd tasteless clothing starts to cause ridicule

indicators.note: one word clothes another, wrapping around it

parts.note: food so tasteless it cannot be eaten is inedible

indicators.note: the starts of the two words cause and ridicule are their first letters

explanation.surface: Wearing outrageously bad-taste clothes invites ridicule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tasteless clothing' reads as bad fashion; 'clothing' is the wrapping signal and 'tasteless' is the food sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absurd is beyond belief, impossible to credit.

clue.text: Bore shed tears about a Republican

indicators.note: the crying goes about the other letters, around them

parts.note: to cry is to shed tears

explanation.surface: A boring person cried over a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a noun for a tedious person; it is the past tense of bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Bore, past tense of bear, means carried.

clue.text: You forget 50 per cent of ideas

indicators.note: forgetting half of the word means dropping its second half and keeping the first four letters

parts.note: thoughts are ideas

explanation.surface: A dig that someone forgets half their ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic second-person pronoun is the old familiar form of you.

clue.text: Gosh! Harbour's invaded by Spain

indicators.note: the harbour is invaded, the other letter entering it

parts.note: a haven is a harbour, with the possessive S
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise as a harbour is invaded by Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavens is an exclamation of surprise, like gosh.

clue.text: Fiasco, using grasping member of family

indicators.note: the words grasp the letters, holding them within

explanation.surface: A greedy relative causes a fiasco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grasping' looks like greedy, describing the relative; it holds the letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A cousin is a relative, child of an aunt or uncle.

clue.text: Serial broadcast in Middle Eastern country

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered abroad, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A TV serial being shown in a Middle Eastern country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serial broadcast' reads as a TV show going out; 'broadcast' scatters the letters of serial.
explanation.definitionFit: The state on the eastern Mediterranean coast is a nation of the Middle East.

clue.text: I admit having no piercing may be stupid

indicators.note: no pierces the other word, going into its middle

parts.note: to grant a point is to admit it

explanation.surface: Someone confesses having no body piercings, which may seem foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piercing' looks like body jewellery, but it is the signal for one word going inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorant is used informally for stupid or uninformed, lacking knowledge.

clue.text: Going north from here, craft regularly vacant

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means read upwards, so the picked letters run backwards
regularly picks every other letter, the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: A boat heading north from here at regular intervals, empty.
explanation.definitionFit: Free can mean unoccupied, as a vacant seat.

clue.text: More curious to tour Italy — it's louder

indicators.note: one word tours round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: nosier means more curious or prying
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A nosier tourist in Italy turns out to be a noisier one.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisier means making more sound, so louder.

clue.text: Hang nudes in new arrangement over small piano

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are laid over the two small pieces, covering them
the word nudes is put in a new arrangement of its letters

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: Hanging nude pictures in a new display above a small piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In new arrangement' turns NUDES into SU...END, which goes over S and P to give SU-SP-END.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend something is to hang it from above.

clue.text: Family take a dip, busy creatures

parts.note: to descend is to go down, take a dip
ants are proverbially busy insects

explanation.surface: A family going for a swim like busy creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take a dip' suggests swimming; it means going down.
explanation.definitionFit: One's descendants, children and grandchildren onwards, are family in the line coming after.
